anchor.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Repair ONE localized furniture/anatomy occlusion error in this exact transparent Qianxia desktop-pet illustration.
The dark navy desk FRONT APRON currently has an impossible arch/notch cut away around her skirt and thighs, making her legs appear to pass THROUGH the desktop. Repair the FRONT APRON into a continuous solid panel across the entire desk width: its LOWER EDGE must be ONE STRAIGHT HORIZONTAL line between the desk legs, at the existing lower-edge level of the left/right apron ends. Fill in the central arched missing section with matching navy panel color/shading. The front apron is physically IN FRONT OF the seated character's skirt, lap, upper thighs and chair. It must occlude all skirt/thigh parts that currently overlap its rectangular area. NO skin or skirt may be drawn on top of the navy apron; no notch, window, curved cutout or knee-shaped hole.
Below that straight front-panel edge, show ONLY the natural lower visible portion of her bent knees, dark socks and small shoes emerging beneath the desk. Keep the pink chair behind her thighs and behind the apron. If necessary move the seat/lap slightly farther back or lower, but preserve small shoe scale and the original overall body proportions. This is an occlusion repair, not amputated disconnected legs; knees and lower legs must remain naturally attached to a concealed seated body. Keep shoes together and fully visible. Do not lengthen legs or enlarge feet. Desk supports stay outside her legs.
Preserve the white desktop surface, cyan front light strip, X sticker, vent slots, desk feet, left bunny, right stacked storage boxes, ALL upper-body pose, face, expression, hair, bow, hands and fan-shaped browser holograms exactly as closely as possible. Do not redesign anything above the apron. Same image composition, clean dark-indigo outlines and colors. One full static PNG, true transparent background, preserve alpha, no captions or checkerboard.
